steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Rust web application. Start in the `/app` Git repository: it has a minimal Cargo project (`quizzy`) and no app yet. Rust (stable), Cargo, SQLite (the library and the CLI), and Chromium are installed. You can download crates from crates.io; other network access is blocked. Fetch and build all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the build, the database, and so on) and runs the app in release mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`. It must work offline (for example, `cargo build --release --offline`), and it should start in a few minutes at most.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

cd /app && python3 - <<'PY' p='src/views.rs';s=open(p).read();s=s.replace('Import quiz', '
');open(p,'w').write(s) PY cat > docs/import-export.md <<'EOF' # Portable quiz contents Moderator navigation: - `/moderate`: **Import quiz** opens `/moderate/quizzes/import`. - Paste JSON into **Quiz JSON** and submit **Import**. Success redirects to a newly created quiz, even if another quiz has the same title. - Each quiz has an **Export** link to `/moderate/quizzes/:id/export`. Its only `
` contains pretty-printed JSON, HTML-escaped for safe copying through
  the browser. Inactive questions are included.

The portable schema contains only `title` and `questions`; each question has
`text`, `active`, and `options`; each option has `text` and `correct`. Both
booleans are always exported. Missing `active` defaults to true; missing
`correct` defaults to false. Types are checked by Serde (null is not a missing
boolean). Required strings and arrays must be present. Unknown properties are
ignored on import and are never re-exported. There are no IDs, positions,
credentials, or runtime/session data in the format. Array order is retained.
An empty quiz is valid, just as one created with the New quiz form is.

`QuizContents::parse` validates the complete payload before any writes. Every
question uses `Draft::errors`, the same validator used by the question form:
nonblank question text, at least two nonblank options, and at least one correct
nonblank option. Like the form, blank option rows are skipped and saved text is
trimmed. Invalid input returns 422 with an error identifying the question and
preserves the submitted JSON for correction.

`QuizContents::insert` owns one SQLite transaction for the quiz and every
question and option. It shares the question writer with form saves, avoiding
normalization differences or nested transactions. Even a database failure
partway through rolls everything back. Existing quizzes are never modified.
All routes use the existing moderator authentication and POST CSRF protection.
No dependencies or schema migrations were added.

## Regression checks

With `bin/serve` running and the test credentials/environment described in
`docs/implementation.md`:

```sh

cargo clippy --offline --locked -- -D warnings
python3 tests/import_export.py
python3 tests/smoke.py
python3 tests/browser.py
python3 tests/persistence.py
```

The import/export HTTP test checks exact schema, ordering, default and explicit
booleans, Unicode/HTML safety, duplicate titles, empty quizzes, normalization,
malformed JSON, invalid types, question rules, authentication, CSRF, error
retention, and no partial quiz creation. The Rust tests also force a database
failure during the second question to verify rollback of all three tables.
The Chromium regression copies the export's DOM text, tries invalid JSON, then
imports and re-exports an identical quiz via the labeled controls, checking
mobile overflow along the way.
